chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The nabbash (grave digger/excavator), if he is known for that (digging up graves), his hand is cut off.

key_terms.النَّبَّاشُ: The grave digger or excavator, specifically one who digs up graves to steal.
key_terms.قُطِعَ: He was cut off (referring to the hand, a standard hudud punishment).

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a grave digger who is known for digging up graves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Ishtibār establishes the hadd punishment of amputation for the nabbash (grave robber) specifically when the act is established through customary knowledge (ma'ruf) rather than requiring two witnesses. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often linked to the concept of 'hudud al-thaniyya' or applied via the principle of 'shuhra' (prevalence of the act), emphasizing the sanctity of the deceased's body and property. The brevity of the text highlights the reliance on juristic interpretation to define the precise conditions under which 'known' status triggers the physical penalty.
